app.title: ClimCanvas
app.summary: A person opens one or more netCDF files (a single file, a wildcard, or a list of files joined along time), and can attach separate coordinate files when needed. They lay out a grid of panels, pick a plot mode for each one (horizontal map, vertical or time section, 1-D line, distribution, scatter or 2-D aggregate), choose the variable, time, level and region, then stack layers such as filled contours, contour lines, hatching and vectors. Under the figure, a box lists every transform, average and mask that was applied. Finally they export the figure as an image, step it through time as a GIF or MP4, or download a standalone Python script that reproduces the figure exactly, and they can save the whole setup as a session.

task.text: Build publication-ready, reproducible multi-panel figures from gridded atmospheric and ocean data, without writing plotting code.

data.text: Gridded model or reanalysis output in netCDF: variables over time, vertical level, latitude and longitude, on regular or curvilinear grids, plus optional point tracks.
data.item: a variable in a netCDF dataset, sliced to a time, a level and a region

stage.text: exploring gridded model output and turning it into figures for a paper

mechanism.text: Sidebar forms build a configuration for each panel: plot mode, slice, projection and a stack of layers. The main area redraws the whole multi-panel figure from that configuration, lists the processing applied, and offers the same configuration as an image, an animation or a reproduction script.

field.text: plotting gridded atmospheric and oceanic data in climate science

workflow.name: build a reproducible multi-panel figure from gridded data

steps.here: type a netCDF path, a wildcard or a .lst file (or browse the allowed folders) and press Add; files split by time are joined along time, and separate lon/lat coordinate files can be attached

steps.step: lay out the panels of the figure
steps.here: set rows and columns or a mosaic string, set width and height ratios, and add, duplicate, reorder or delete panels; a shared-edit mode copies changes to every panel

steps.step: choose the view and the slice for each panel
steps.here: pick a plot mode (map, vertical section, time section, 1-D, distribution, scatter, 2-D aggregate), then the time, level, region or section path, the projection and the averages over a range
add filled contours, contour lines, hatching, vectors, streamlines, point scatter or tracks, each with its own variable, colormap, levels, value transform and mask

steps.step: check what processing went into the result
steps.here: the figure redraws, and a box beneath it lists value transforms, range averages with their weights and missing-value counts, masks and fixed times for each panel
download PNG, TIFF, SVG, PDF or EPS at a chosen dpi, a GIF or MP4 stepped through time or a rotating globe, a Python script that reproduces the figure exactly, and the session as JSON

distinctive: every figure can be exported as a standalone xarray/matplotlib/cartopy script that is tested to reproduce the app's image pixel for pixel
a 'processing applied to this figure' box lists the transforms, cos(lat)-weighted averages and masks behind the values shown
vertical sections can follow a parallel, a meridian or a great circle with bilinear interpolation, and can hide extrapolated values below the ground with a terrain mask
map projections and curvilinear model grids, with the grid's projection inferred from its 2-D coordinates
animations step every panel through time together, and a layer can be held at a fixed time from another file
